# The Alien's Guide to Earth

> A free, independent study guide that explains great investors, the history of the universe, the evolution of life and basic money ideas in plain words. Written for curious beginners. Education only; not investment advice.

Every summary is written in the site's own words; exact quotations are short and sourced, with links to the originals. Text written for the site is CC BY 4.0.

## Sections

- [Great investors (interactive)](https://alienspacex.com/): 33 investors across the USA, UK, China, India, Japan and the wider world, plus traders
- [The Lemonade Stand](https://alienspacex.com/economics/): profit, cash and the three financial reports explained with a children's lemonade stand
- [From the Big Bang to You](https://alienspacex.com/space/): 13.8 billion years of cosmic history in one scroll
- [From the First Cell to You](https://alienspacex.com/evolution/): the story of life and human evolution
- [All pages](https://alienspacex.com/library.html): every investor and every big idea, as plain text pages

## For AI agents

- [Full text of every investor and trader page](https://alienspacex.com/llms-full.txt): one plain-text file
- [Structured index (JSON)](https://alienspacex.com/api/people.json): names, summaries, big ideas, page and source links
- [RSS feed](https://alienspacex.com/feed.xml): new pages and corrections, newest first
- Every investor page has a Markdown twin at https://alienspacex.com/md/<id>.md, for example https://alienspacex.com/md/buffett.md
- Please cite the page URL; text written for this site is CC BY 4.0. Quotations stay with their authors.

## Investors and traders

### USA

- [Warren Buffett](https://alienspacex.com/buffett.html): Ran Berkshire Hathaway for sixty years and explained every decision in a yearly letter to its owners.
- [Charlie Munger](https://alienspacex.com/munger.html): Buffett's partner for over forty years, and the clearest thinker on why smart people make bad decisions.
- [Peter Lynch](https://alienspacex.com/lynch.html): Ran the Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, beat the market by a mile, and showed ordinary people how to find good stocks.
- [Benjamin Graham](https://alienspacex.com/graham.html): Taught Buffett, wrote the two founding books of value investing, and turned a near-ruinous 1929 into rules for never being ruined again.
- [Philip Fisher](https://alienspacex.com/fisher.html): Ran his own firm for 68 years, found great companies by talking to everyone around them, and held Motorola for nearly half a century.
- [John Templeton](https://alienspacex.com/templeton.html): Bought 104 cheap shares as war broke out in 1939, then searched the whole world for bargains at the point of maximum pessimism.
- [John Bogle](https://alienspacex.com/bogle.html): Launched the first index fund for ordinary investors, was mocked for it, and spent his life cutting the costs that eat savers' returns.
- [Howard Marks](https://alienspacex.com/marks.html): Has written memos since 1990 that Buffett opens first: on risk, cycles, and thinking differently from the crowd.
- [Seth Klarman](https://alienspacex.com/klarman.html): Wrote a book that sold 5,000 copies and became a legend, and built a firm on one rule above all: avoid losing money.
- [Walter Schloss](https://alienspacex.com/schloss.html): Never went to college, never visited a company, owned a hundred cheap shares at a time, and beat the market for 47 years.

### UK

- [Anthony Bolton](https://alienspacex.com/bolton.html): Ran Fidelity Special Situations for 28 years, about 19.5% a year, by buying good companies the crowd had given up on.
- [Terry Smith](https://alienspacex.com/smith.html): Exposed creative accounting and lost his job for it, then built Fundsmith on three rules: buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing.
- [John Maynard Keynes](https://alienspacex.com/keynes.html): The century's most famous economist failed at forecasting markets, changed his method, and beat the UK market for a quarter of a century.

### China

- [Li Lu](https://alienspacex.com/lilu.html): Heard Buffett speak by chance, founded Himalaya Capital, and became the only outside manager Charlie Munger said he ever invested with.
- [Duan Yongping](https://alienspacex.com/duan.html): Built the companies behind OPPO and vivo, then turned investor: buy businesses you understand, never borrow, and keep a list of things you won't do.
- [Qiu Guolu](https://alienspacex.com/qiu.html): Boiled investing down to three questions, why cheap, why good, why now, and built one of China's largest private fund firms on them.
- [Zhang Lei](https://alienspacex.com/zhanglei.html): Learned investing at Yale under David Swensen, founded Hillhouse with $20 million, and preaches long-term bets on great entrepreneurs.

### India

- [Chandrakant Sampat](https://alienspacex.com/sampat.html): India's original value investor: left the family business in the 1950s, bought the Indian arms of global companies cheaply, and taught a generation.
- [Parag Parikh](https://alienspacex.com/parikh.html): Started as a sub-broker in 1979, became India's voice of behavioural finance, and built a fund with one scheme and his own money in it.
- [Radhakishan Damani](https://alienspacex.com/damani.html): Dalal Street's famous bear turned patient investor, then built DMart from one Mumbai store on low costs, owned shops and fast payments.

### Japan

- [Seiroku Honda](https://alienspacex.com/honda.html): A poor farmer's son who saved a quarter of every pay cheque from 25, invested it, and gave almost all of it away when he retired.
- [Wahei Takeda](https://alienspacex.com/takeda.html): Made Japan's favourite baby biscuit, then became a patient shareholder in over a hundred companies, treating each as a field to tend.
- [Atsuto Sawakami](https://alienspacex.com/sawakami.html): Founded Japan's first independent fund company in 1999 and preached long-term investing for decades, when few in Japan would listen.

### World

- [Prem Watsa](https://alienspacex.com/watsa.html): Reached Canada from Hyderabad with almost nothing, turned a failing insurer into Fairfax, and grew its book value 18.7% a year for forty years.
- [Francisco García Paramés](https://alienspacex.com/parames.html): Taught himself value investing from Peter Lynch and Buffett's letters, then beat Spain's market for 21 years, survived his worst years, and kept going.
- [André Kostolany](https://alienspacex.com/kostolany.html): A speculator, not a value investor: rich twice, broke in between, and the man who taught Germany how crowds move markets.
- [Peter Cundill](https://alienspacex.com/cundill.html): Read Graham on a plane in 1973, then hunted the world for shares below their liquidation value: the Indiana Jones of Canadian money managers.
- [Luiz Barsi Filho](https://alienspacex.com/barsi.html): Shined shoes in a São Paulo tenement, then built his own pension one dividend share at a time, and became Brazil's biggest individual investor.
- [Allan Gray](https://alienspacex.com/gray.html): Rose 10% at Fidelity while the 1962 market crashed, founded South Africa's biggest private fund firm and Orbis, then gave his control to charity.
- [Cheah Cheng Hye](https://alienspacex.com/cheah.html): Sold pineapples as a boy in Penang, spent 17 years as a journalist, then built Value Partners from under US$5 million: Asia's Warren Buffett.

### Traders

- [Paul Tudor Jones](https://alienspacex.com/ptj.html): Lost most of his clients' money on one cotton trade in 1979, built his rules around defence, and made a reported 125.9% after fees in 1987, the year of the crash.
- [Mark Minervini](https://alienspacex.com/minervini.html): Lost all his capital in the 1980s, then studied history's biggest winning stocks and won the U.S. Investing Championship twice, in 1997 and 2021.
- [Stanley Druckenmiller](https://alienspacex.com/druckenmiller.html): Ran George Soros's Quantum Fund, came up with the 1992 bet against the pound, and reported about 30% a year at his own fund without a losing year.
